newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bank of Thailand says considering loan definition.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Thailand says considering loan definition.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand may allow lenders to carry fully collateralised non-performing loans to viable debtors for another six months without categorising the debt as sub-standard, a senior official told Reuters.

"If it is found that the performance of the debtor is not viable we will ask the financial institution to classify it as sub-standard, but if we think the project of the debtor is still viable we may allow the financial institution to accrue the interest for another six months up to a 12 month maximum," the central bank official said.
The definition remains under discussion and the bank would consult with major lenders' associations before coming to a conclusion, the central bank executive said.
"We are yet to finalise the definition on this one, we have to carefully study this issue," he said.
"The bank ... will meet with the Association of Finance Companies and the Thai Bankers Association to finalise the definition very soon," he added.
Earlier this year the central bank asked financial institutions to make increased provisions for sub-standard loans to help stabilise the sector.

Investors have grown concerned about deteriorating loan portfolio quality among Thai lenders given slowing economic growth this year and oversupply in a property market now threatened by declining asset values.

Under the toughened provisioning requirements, commercial banks were asked to make provisions for 15 percent of their sub-standard debts, and finance companies have to make provisions for 20 percent of sub-standard debts.
Some firms complained the increased provisioning requirements would adversely affect profitability.
As part of confidence restoring measures, the central bank has asked financial institutions to declare non-performing loan data at the end of the second quarter.
